requirements.title: An OPTIONAL entity must be a dummy argument
requirements.definition: An entity with OPTIONAL must be a dummy argument. Eligible dummy data objects and dummy procedures retain their other attribute/interface rules. Unlike INTENT's procedure restriction, this does not require every optional dummy procedure to be a procedure pointer.

Complete eligible data/procedure admissions and minimally repaired nondummy declarations, with source-specific role diagnostics.

C851 ordinary OPTIONAL eligibility family: four complete compile/f2023 cases form two diagnostic/positive-control pairs. An external subroutine declares ordinary INTEGER OPTIONAL subject, and a module-contained procedure declares ordinary nonpointer PROCEDURE(signature) OPTIONAL callback with a prior abstract subroutine interface. Each invalid omits its subject from the dummy list; the sole repair inserts that name in the existing procedure header, preserving all other bytes. The actual staged declarations at lines3 and10 contain OPTIONAL and no INTENT or VALUE, so the exact measured GNU nondummy-role error and Flang full attribute/nondummy-role warning identify this predicate. A report must match a complete extracted cause at its actual staged subject declaration; generic argument words, echoes and foreign origins do not qualify. Only the observed exact Flang warning is a nonfatal allowance. Both controls require successful object compilation and retain positive-control evidence, not runtime effect.
requirements.oracle_limitation:
Required reporting capability is not fatal exit, standardized wording or a printed code. No broad INTENT-style procedure-pointer limitation is imported, and unrelated attribute/interface failures cannot qualify.

C851 ordinary OPTIONAL eligibility limits: this family represents only data-dummy-admission, procedure-dummy-admission and nondummy-exclusion. It is not an exhaustive C851 case census. The callback repair remains a nonpointer dummy procedure, without INTENT, POINTER, initialization or SAVE. There are no calls, allocation, association, VALUE, C/coarray, payload or runtime operations. Entry/other-attribute boundaries and all S8.5.12-001 plans retain their independently managed states. The PRESENT note supplies no new case or source-use/runtime credit. Reporting capability does not prescribe fatal status, English wording or a printed code; these finite exact messages are calibrated qualification routes, not a universal vocabulary. No additional source span is needed by the measured reports, and neither coalesced lines nor widened spans are used. Unsupported procedures, Internal/ASR/crash/resource failures, quoted examples, source echoes and wrong-file reports never count. Flang f2018 evidence is not relabelled f2023. Generation preserves unselected pending/control and all review records, without approving, renewing, retagging or updating a baseline.

requirements.title: OPTIONAL permits a procedure reference without an effective argument for the dummy
requirements.definition: An OPTIONAL dummy need not have an effective argument in a procedure reference. This admission is subject to exact argument correspondence, an explicit interface where required,15.5.2.13 presence/absence and permitted-use rules, and the dummy's other attributes. It is not a definition that presence, allocation, pointer association and having an effective argument are equivalent.

pending.omitted-data-actual: PENDING a complete internal/module procedure with an ordinary OPTIONAL data dummy, called both with a defined actual and without it. pending.dummy-category-controls: PENDING omitted eligible ALLOCATABLE, data-pointer, nonpointer dummy-procedure and procedure-pointer actual contexts. Presence checks do not permit dereferencing, invoking, allocating or changing an absent dummy. Complete controls retain valid interfaces and do not presume initial pointer status.
pending.forwarded-absence-source: PENDING canonical15.5.2.13p1/p3/p4 relations for forwarding an absent optional dummy to an optional recipient. Preserve exceptions, subobject-selector exclusions and pointer/allocatable recipient-category restrictions. No duplicate actual or arbitrary forwarding to a required dummy is admitted.
pending.presence-state-source: PENDING the exact absence branches for an unallocated allocatable or disassociated pointer actual corresponding to a dummy without those attributes, versus present attributed dummy contexts. Use normative16.9.163 for PRESENT and its name/host-accessibility condition. Unallocated, disassociated, undefined and absent are not interchangeable states.
pending.conditional-nil-source: PENDING source/fixture relations to15.5.1 R1526-R1528/C1540-C1545 and15.5.2.3: a chosen .NIL. yields a not-present actual. Every consequent-arg still meets the dummy's evaluation-independent type/kind/attribute requirements. Do not treat .NIL. as a standalone null pointer or skip unchosen-consequent constraints.
